tickers.reason: Delta Air Lines — best-in-class US airline and the cleanest DE-ESCALATION hedge for a book that is otherwise 100% conflict-long. June 11 thesis flip: Trump cancelled strikes, declared a 'great settlement,' deal may sign Sunday with Hormuz reopening within 30 days; Brent broke <$90 (threshold breached), WTI ~$84. Jet fuel is Delta's #2 cost and ran ~2x YoY during the war — every $1 Brent decline drops straight to margin. Owns the Monroe refinery (~$300M Q2 in-house fuel benefit). Strong Buy consensus (56% Strong Buy/44% Buy), median PT $80 vs ~$68 spot, Morgan Stanley PT $105 (June 1). Catalyst: Q2 earnings July 9 2026 — first read on fuel relief. Replaces DHT: the tanker's record-Q2-VLCC-rate catalyst is now directly invalidated by the 30-day Hormuz-reopening clause in the draft deal (Evercore already cut FRO to In Line PT $38; Brief flagged tankers as the single most exposed corner of the watchlist).

AeroVironment — loitering-munitions leader (Switchblade 300/600) and the cleanest defense / Iran-re-escalation play. Trades $172.93 vs 52wk high $417.86 (~59% drawdown), bottom of range ($156 low). HARD DATED CATALYST: FY26 Q4/full-year earnings June 30 2026 (consensus Q4 EPS ~$1.89, FY ~$3.36, FY26 rev guide $1.95-2.0B, $4.6B+ backlog of re-awards YTD). Direct exposure to the exact Iran drone/missile exchange driving the June 13-14 re-escalation tail (signing slipped, Hormuz military activity, Beirut strike). Buy consensus (avg PT ~$310, some Street $400+). Replaces KTOS: same defense / re-escalation thesis but AVAV is the larger, more liquid pure-play loitering-munitions leader with a harder near-term catalyst (dated June 30 earnings vs KTOS diffuse award flow) and a deeper drawdown for better risk/reward. Structural rearmament backstop survives de-escalation.

Newmont Corporation — World's largest gold miner. Q1 2026 EPS $2.90 vs $2.24 est (29% beat). Record $3.1B FCF on $4,900/oz realized gold. Revenue $7.31B (+42% YoY). Analyst PTs $129-145 (20-35% upside from $107). Gold structural bull market ($5,000-6,000 targets). Fills critical safe-haven/gold blind spot — watchlist has ZERO precious metals exposure. Works in escalation AND de-escalation.

Valero Energy — Largest independent US refiner (~3.2 Mbpd), ~40% distillate-weighted output. THE de-escalation-resilient conflict play: 3-2-1 crack spread holding ~$40/bbl even as Brent fell to ~$97 — refiners WIN on cheaper feedstock if Hormuz reopens while product premiums persist (capacity closures + distillate tightness). Buy consensus (17-20 analysts). Q2 2026 earnings (~late July) the catalyst. Replaces STNG to cut tanker double-weight (DHT+STNG) as de-escalation risk rose materially: oil down ~20% from 2026 peak, Lebanon ceasefire, Trump 60-day Hormuz MOU framework.

Phillips 66 — diversified downstream (refining ~30-35% of earnings + midstream + 50% CPChem JV) and the cleanest DE-ESCALATION-RESILIENT play for a conflict-long book. June 13 binary weekend: US-Iran peace deal final text agreed, signing expected ~Sun June 14 in Geneva, Hormuz reopens within 30 days, Brent crashed to ~$87 (sub-$90 threshold breached). Refining margins typically EXPAND when crude falls (cheaper feedstock, sticky product cracks), and the midstream fee-based segment ($591M Q1) is commodity-price-agnostic — so PSX works on de-escalation where oil E&P/tankers/defense reverse. IDIOSYNCRATIC CATALYST INDEPENDENT OF MACRO: Elliott's 'Streamline 66' campaign — nominated 4 directors, pushing a midstream-divestiture sum-of-parts breakup targeting >$200/share. Buy consensus, avg PT ~$166 (Goldman $207 May 19, Mizuho upgrade to Outperform May 27). Q2 earnings ~late July catalyst. Replaces CF: the fertilizer thesis (~50% of seaborne urea transits Hormuz → nitrogen stays tight) is directly INVALIDATED by the 30-day Hormuz-reopening clause — same de-escalation logic that retired the DHT tanker on June 12.
